title: “In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim” — yet the word is sent to kings through Zedekiah
summary: Jeremiah 27 opens by dating the word to the start of Jehoiakim’s reign, then sends the yokes by messengers who come “unto Zedekiah king of Judah” (27:3), and 27:12 says Jeremiah spoke the same words to Zedekiah. The chapter names two kings of Judah in one message. Brenton’s Greek prints no verse 1: its page begins at verse 2.
text: KJV Jeremiah 27:1: “In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah came this word unto Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,” KJV 27:3: “And send them to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the Ammonites, and to the king of Tyrus, and to the king of Zidon, by the hand of the messengers which come to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah king of Judah;” KJV 27:12: “I spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.” Hebrew (WLC) 27:1: בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהֹויָקִ֥ם בֶּן־יֹאושִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔ה מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ Hebrew (WLC) 27:12: וְאֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי כְּכָל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹ֑ר הָבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־צַוְּארֵיכֶ֜ם בְּעֹ֣ל מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֗ל וְעִבְד֥וּ אֹתֹ֛ו וְעַמֹּ֖ו וִֽחְיֽוּ׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek, printed as Jeremiah 34): the page prints verses 2 to 6, 8 to 12, 14 to 16, 18 to 20 and 22, and 27:1 is not among them; its verse 3 reads Καὶ ἀποστελεῖς αὐτοὺς πρὸς βασιλέα Ἰδουμαίας, καὶ πρὸς βασιλέα Μωὰβ, καὶ πρὸς βασιλέα υἱῶν Ἀμμὼν, καὶ πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα Τύρου, καὶ πρὸς βασιλέα Σιδῶνος, ἐν χερσὶν ἀγγέλων αὐτῶν τῶν ἐρχομένων εἰς ἀπάντησιν αὐτῶν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ πρὸς Σεδεκίαν βασιλέα Ἰούδα. and its verse 12 reads Καὶ πρὸς Σεδεκίαν βασιλέα Ἰούδα ἐλάλησα κατὰ πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους, λέγων, εἰσαγάγετε τὸν τράχηλον ὑμῶν. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER27.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/27/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER34.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew of 27:1 names Jehoiakim (יְהוֹיָקִים) and the KJV agrees with it. The message in the same chapter is addressed to the messengers who come to Zedekiah (27:3) and, in 27:12, Jeremiah says he spoke to Zedekiah “according to all these words”. Jehoiakim and Zedekiah are different kings of Judah, so the chapter carries two dates. In the Greek page quoted there is no opening verse and Zedekiah is the only king named in the verses printed, so the clash does not appear there.
scope: T applies at 27:1 only (the verse the Greek page does not print). The clash is inside the Hebrew and the KJV between 27:1 and 27:3, 27:12. The two statements could be reconciled if the word first came under Jehoiakim and was repeated to the envoys and to Zedekiah later; the text does not report that. The record does not say which reading is original, and the Greek page not printing a verse does not show that the verse was absent from every Greek manuscript. A digital edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees, and this record compares the wording of the texts and does not show which reading is original.

title: “All nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son’s son” and “restore them to this place” — the Greek page has neither
summary: The KJV has two statements at 27:7 and 27:22 that Brenton’s Greek page (printed as Jeremiah 34) does not give: that the nations serve Nebuchadnezzar, his son and his son’s son until his own time comes, and that the temple vessels carried to Babylon will be brought up and restored. The Greek page prints no verse 7, and its verse 22 ends at “they shall go into Babylon”.
text: KJV Jeremiah 27:7: “And all nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son's son, until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.” KJV 27:22: “They shall be carried to Babylon, and there shall they be until the day that I visit them, saith the Lord; then will I bring them up, and restore them to this place.” Hebrew (WLC) 27:7: וְעָבְד֤וּ אֹתֹו֙ כָּל־הַגֹּויִ֔ם וְאֶת־בְּנֹ֖ו וְאֶֽת־בֶּן־בְּנֹ֑ו עַ֣ד בֹּא־עֵ֤ת אַרְצֹו֙ גַּם־ה֔וּא וְעָ֤בְדוּ בֹו֙ גֹּויִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים וּמְלָכִ֖ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃ Hebrew (WLC) 27:22: בָּבֶ֥לָה יוּבָ֖אוּ וְשָׁ֣מָּה יִֽהְי֑וּ עַ֠ד יֹ֣ום פָּקְדִ֤י אֹתָם֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְהַֽעֲלִיתִים֙ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔ים אֶל־הַמָּקֹ֖ום הַזֶּֽה׃  פ Septuagint (Brenton Greek, printed as Jeremiah 34): the page prints verses 2 to 6, 8 to 12, 14 to 16, 18 to 20 and 22; verse 6 is followed by verse 8, and verse 22 reads εἰς Βαβυλῶνα εἰσελεύσεται, λέγει Κύριος. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER27.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/27/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER34.htm.
reasoning: In the KJV and the Hebrew the dominion is limited in time (“his son, and his son’s son, until the very time of his land come”) and the exile of the vessels is limited in time (“until the day that I visit them … then will I bring them up, and restore them”). In the Greek page quoted, the first limit is not stated, and the vessels are said to go into Babylon with no return stated in the verse. The Greek page does repeat, at its verse 16, the prophets’ claim that the vessels “shall return from Babylon”, but there it is the claim the Lord calls false, not the Lord’s own promise.
scope: T applies at 27:7 and at 27:22, as omissions on the Greek page named. The record does not say the Greek text denies a return; it says the page prints no such statement at these verses. The difference is between the KJV and the Greek page, and the Hebrew is quoted to show what the KJV renders. The page’s verse 22 may simply be shorter. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees, and this record compares the wording of the texts and does not show which reading is original.

title: The promise that “David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne” — the Greek page ends at verse 13
summary: In the KJV the chapter continues after verse 13 with the promise of the Branch, that David shall never want a man on the throne, and that the Levites shall not want a man before the Lord (33:14-26). Brenton’s Greek page for the chapter (printed as Jeremiah 40) ends at verse 13 and prints none of these thirteen verses.
text: KJV Jeremiah 33:17-18: “For thus saith the Lord; David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel;” “Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.” KJV 33:22: “As the host of heaven cannot be numbered, neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant, and the Levites that minister unto me.” Hebrew (WLC) 33:17: כִּי־כֹ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֣ת לְדָוִ֔ד אִ֕ישׁ יֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֥א בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek, printed as Jeremiah 40): the page prints verses 1 to 13; verse 13 reads ἐν πόλεσι τῆς ὀρεινῆς, καὶ ἐν πόλεσι τῆς σεφηλὰ, καὶ ἐν πόλεσι τῆς ναγὲβ, καὶ ἐν γῇ Βενιαμὶν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς κύκλῳ Ἱερουσαλὴμ, καὶ ἐν πόλεσιν Ἰούδα· ἔτι παρελεύσεται πρόβατα ἐπὶ χεῖρα ἀριθμοῦντος, εἶπε Κύριος. and the page then ends. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER33.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/33/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER40.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew and the KJV give a standing promise about the throne of David and the priests the Levites at 33:17-22, and a rebuttal of the people’s saying that the Lord has cast off the two families at 33:24-26. The Greek page quoted prints none of it, so a reader of that page does not meet the promise that David shall not lack a man on the throne or the promise about the Levites in this chapter.
scope: T applies at 33:14–26 as an omission on the Greek page named, and the record names 33:17, 33:18 and 33:22 as the verses carrying the specific promises. It compares what the pages print and does not show how the passage came to be shorter or longer. Other Greek chapters may state a promise about David; this record does not claim otherwise. title: “In the ninth year of Zedekiah … in the tenth month” — the Greek has “the ninth month” and no year
summary: The KJV and the Hebrew date Nebuchadnezzar’s arrival at Jerusalem to the ninth year of Zedekiah and the tenth month. Brenton’s Greek (printed as Jeremiah 46:1) has the ninth month of Zedekiah and no year.
text: KJV Jeremiah 39:1: “In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, came Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army against Jerusalem, and they besieged it.” Hebrew (WLC) 39:1: בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠תְּשִׁעִית לְצִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֜ה בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂרִ֗י בָּ֠א נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֨ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֤ל וְכָל־חֵילֹו֙ אֶל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיָּצֻ֖רוּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃    ס Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Jeremiah 46:1: Καὶ ἐγένετο τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἐννάτῳ τοῦ Σεδεκία βασιλέως Ἰούδα, παρεγένετο Ναβουχοδονόσορ βασιλεὺς Βαβυλῶνος, καὶ πᾶσα ἡ δύναμις αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ Ἱερουσαλὴμ, καὶ ἐπολιόρκουν αὐτήν. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER39.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/39/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER46.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew has בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂרִי “in the tenth month” and בַּשָּׁנָה הַתְּשִׁעִית “in the ninth year”. The Greek has τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἐννάτῳ “in the ninth month” and no year. The month number differs (tenth against ninth) and the year is not given in the Greek.
scope: T applies at 39:1 only. The record compares the wording of the texts at this verse; it does not set the Greek against any parallel, and it does not say which month the siege began in. title: Jeremiah went to Benjamin “to separate himself thence” — the Greek has “to buy”
summary: The KJV says Jeremiah went to the land of Benjamin “to separate himself thence in the midst of the people”. Brenton’s Greek (printed as Jeremiah 44:12) says he went “to buy thence in the midst of the people”.
text: KJV Jeremiah 37:12: “Then Jeremiah went forth out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to separate himself thence in the midst of the people.” Hebrew (WLC) 37:12: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יִרְמְיָ֙הוּ֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לָלֶ֖כֶת אֶ֣רֶץ בִּנְיָמִ֑ן לַחֲלִ֥ק מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּתֹ֥וךְ הָעָֽם׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Jeremiah 44:12: ἐξῆλθεν Ἱερεμίας ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλὴμ τοῦ πορευθῆναι εἰς γῆν Βενιαμεὶν, τοῦ ἀγοράσαι ἐκεῖθεν ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ λαοῦ· Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER37.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/37/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER44.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew infinitive לַחֲלִק (la-ḥălōq) is rendered in the KJV by a verb of withdrawing, “to separate himself”. The Greek τοῦ ἀγοράσαι means “to buy”, an act of trade. The two renderings name different purposes for the journey.
scope: T applies at 37:12 only. The record compares the purposes given; it does not say what the Hebrew word means beyond the two renderings, and the KJV’s “separate” may be one fair reading of the Hebrew. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees.

title: Four men “heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken” — the Greek names three, with different fathers
summary: The KJV and the Hebrew name four men: Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashur son of Malchiah. Brenton’s Greek (printed as Jeremiah 45:1) names three: Saphanias son of Nathan, Godolias son of Pashchor and Joachal son of Semelias.
text: KJV Jeremiah 38:1: “Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people, saying,” Hebrew (WLC) 38:1: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע שְׁפַטְיָ֣ה בֶן־מַתָּ֗ן וּגְדַלְיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־פַּשְׁח֔וּר וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן־שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן־מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה אֶ֨ת־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃    ס Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Jeremiah 45:1: Καὶ ἤκουσε Σαφανίας υἱὸς Νάθαν, καὶ Γοδολίας υἱὸς Πασχὼρ, καὶ Ἰωάχαλ υἱὸς Σεμελίου, τοὺς λόγους οὓς Ἱερεμίας ἐλάλει ἐπὶ τὸν λαὸν, λέγων, Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER38.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/38/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER45.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew lists four men and four fathers. The Greek lists three. The fourth man in the Hebrew, Pashur son of Malchiah (פַּשְׁחוּר בֶּן־מַלְכִּיָּה), has no match in the Greek verse, and the three that remain are spelled differently from the Hebrew (Saphanias, Joachal and so on).
scope: T applies at 38:1 only. The record compares the number of men named; spelling differences between Greek and Hebrew forms of one name are not offered as a finding. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees.

title: The Rechabites fled “for fear of the army of the Syrians” — the Greek has “the Assyrians”
summary: The Rechabites say they came to Jerusalem for fear of two armies. The KJV and the Hebrew name the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram (rendered “Syrians”). Brenton’s Greek (printed as Jeremiah 42:11) names the Chaldeans and the Assyrians (τῶν Ἀσσυρίων).
text: KJV Jeremiah 35:11: “But it came to pass, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up into the land, that we said, Come, and let us go to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians: so we dwell at Jerusalem.” Hebrew (WLC) 35:11: וַיְהִ֗י בַּעֲלֹ֨ות נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֮ אֶל־הָאָרֶץ֒ וַנֹּ֗אמֶר בֹּ֚אוּ וְנָבֹ֣וא יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִפְּנֵי֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּמִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֑ם וַנֵּ֖שֶׁב בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃  פ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Jeremiah 42:11: Καὶ ἐγενήθη ὅτε ἀνέβη Ναβουχοδονόσορ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ εἴπαμεν εἰσελθεῖν, καὶ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ, ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς δυνάμεως τῶν Χαλδαίων, καὶ ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς δυνάμεως τῶν Ἀσσυρίων, καὶ ᾠκοῦμεν ἐκεῖ. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER35.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/35/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER42.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew has חֵיל אֲרָם “the army of Aram”. The Greek has δυνάμεως τῶν Ἀσσυρίων “the force of the Assyrians”. Aram and Assyria are different peoples, so the second army is named differently. “Syrians” in the KJV matches Aram.
scope: T applies at 35:11 only. The record compares the nation named. It does not say which army the Rechabites feared, and the KJV’s “Syrians” is a fair rendering of the Hebrew; the difference is with the Greek. title: “None of them shall remain or escape” in Egypt — and “a small number that escape the sword shall return”
summary: Jeremiah tells the remnant that all who go to Egypt will die and none will remain or escape (42:17). In the Egypt oracle, 44:14 says none of the remnant shall escape or remain, “for none shall return but such as shall escape”, and 44:28 says a small number that escape the sword shall return to the land of Judah.
text: KJV Jeremiah 42:17: “So shall it be with all the men that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: and none of them shall remain or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them.” KJV 44:14: “So that none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah, to the which they have a desire to return to dwell there: for none shall return but such as shall escape.” KJV 44:28: “Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or their's.” Hebrew (WLC) 42:17: וְיִֽהְי֣וּ כָל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֨מוּ אֶת־פְּנֵיהֶ֜ם לָבֹ֤וא מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם יָמ֕וּתוּ בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ שָׂרִ֣יד וּפָלִ֔יט מִפְּנֵי֙ הָֽרָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י מֵבִ֥יא עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃    ס Hebrew (WLC) 44:14: וְלֹ֨א יִהְיֶ֜ה פָּלִ֤יט וְשָׂרִיד֙ לִשְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה הַבָּאִ֥ים לָגֽוּר־שָׁ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלָשׁ֣וּב ׀ אֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֜מָּה מְנַשְּׂאִ֤ים אֶת־נַפְשָׁם֙ לָשׁוּב֙ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת שָׁ֔ם כִּ֥י לֹֽא־יָשׁ֖וּבוּ כִּ֥י אִם־פְּלֵטִֽים׃    ס Hebrew (WLC) 44:28: וּפְלִיטֵ֨י חֶ֜רֶב יְשֻׁב֨וּן מִן־אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָ֖ה מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֑ר וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כָּל־שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה הַבָּאִ֤ים לְאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם דְּבַר־מִ֥י יָק֖וּם מִמֶּ֥נִּי וּמֵהֶֽם׃ Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER42.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER44.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/42/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/44/.
reasoning: At 42:17 and 44:14 the pair is the same: שָׂרִיד וּפָלִיט “remnant and escapee”, none of which shall be. At 44:14 the same verse adds that none shall return except פְּלֵטִים “escapees”, and 44:28 says פְּלִיטֵי חֶרֶב “those who escape the sword” shall return, few in number. The word for escapee is denied at 42:17 and 44:14a and granted at 44:14b and 44:28.
scope: No tag: the finding is inside the Hebrew and the KJV and no translation difference is claimed. The statements can both stand if “escape” in the denials means escape from the judgment in Egypt and the exceptions are those who leave Egypt, which 44:14 and 44:28 appear to say; the text does not report who the few are. The record does not say the passage is in error.
